questions.q: What is a procedure, as the lesson defines the third layer beneath policy and standard?
options: The step-by-step operational instructions for actually doing what a standard requires
A synonym for policy with no real difference
A legal document only lawyers are allowed to write
A tool used to measure governance program budgets
questions.explain: The procedure is the concrete how-to layer underneath the standard's checkable rule and the policy's stated requirement.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a "working," checkable standard rather than a weak one?
options: "Customer PII fields must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or stronger"
"Customer data should be reasonably protected"
"We care deeply about customer privacy"
"Data should generally be kept secure"
questions.explain: A checkable standard names a specific, verifiable rule that can be answered yes or no — the vaguer options can't be.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say procedures are where most employees actually experience governance?
options: Most employees rarely read policy or standard documents, but they follow procedures constantly without necessarily realizing it's governance
Procedures are legally required reading for every employee annually
Standards and policies are never written down anywhere
Procedures replace the need for any policy or standard
questions.explain: The lesson notes procedures are the operational layer people actually interact with day to day, unlike the higher-altitude policy and standard documents.

questions.q: According to the three-layer table, which layer changes most often?
options: Procedure, since it changes as tools and systems change
Policy, since it changes constantly
Standard, since it never changes once written
All three layers change at exactly the same rate
questions.explain: The table shows policy rarely changes, standard changes occasionally as technology changes, and procedure changes most often as tools change.

questions.q: What does the lesson mean by each layer having its own "altitude"?
options: Policy, standard, and procedure each answer a different question and shouldn't duplicate each other's content
Governance documents must be physically stored at different office locations
Only senior executives are allowed to read policy documents
Altitude refers to how many pages each document type must have
questions.explain: The lesson's altitude principle is about keeping each layer focused on its own question — what/why, exactly what, and how — without restating the others.
